Your member profile lives on this wiki and shows up on the Members page. It takes about 5 minutes. warning Do NOT edit TEMPLATE.md directly. It is a read-only template. You must copy it to a new file and edit your copy.

You will touch 3 files: File What to do docs/about/members/your-name.md Create — copy the template, fill in your details src/data/members.ts Edit — add your entry so the grid card appears sidebars.ts Edit — add your page to the sidebar
Go to fossunited.org and create your profile. Set a profile photo there — your wiki photo is pulled automatically from your FOSS United account.
Click "Fork" at the top right of saiufosswiki, then clone your fork locally.

cp docs/about/members/TEMPLATE.md docs/about/members/your-name.md Open docs/about/members/your-name.md and replace the entire file with: --- title: Your Full Name sidebar_label: Your Full Name --- import { useMemberPhoto } from '@site/src/hooks/useMemberPhoto'; export function YourProfile() { const { photoUrl } = useMemberPhoto('your-fossunited-username', 'your-github-username'); return (

); } ## About Write a short paragraph about yourself — what you study, what you're interested in, and what got you into FOSS. --- *Contributing to the SAIU FOSS Wiki since 2025.* Replace all the placeholder values (your-github-username, your-fossunited-username, Your Full Name, Batch 20XX, etc.) with your real info.

Open src/data/members.ts and add an entry to the members array: { name: 'Your Full Name', role: 'Member', // or 'Core Member' batch: 2028, slug: 'your-name', // must match your .md filename (without extension) github: 'your-github-username', fossunited: 'your-fossunited-username', linkedin: 'your-linkedin-username', // optional order: 6, // next number after the last member isCore: false, // true only for core members }, danger The slug must match your .md filename exactly (without the .md extension). If your file is john-doe.md, the slug must be 'john-doe'.
Open sidebars.ts and add your page ID to the "About the Club" category: 'about/members/your-name', // matches your .md filename
npm run start Visit http://localhost:3000/saiufosswiki/about/members/your-name to check your page, and /about/members/ to see your card in the grid.
Push your branch and open a PR against main. A maintainer will review and merge it — usually within a few days. Once merged, your profile appears on the Members page automatically.

documents.s: Decoding Life: Understanding AlphaFold & Protein Folding

documents.t: The FOSS Club explored the exciting intersection of AI, Computer Science, and Biology through a student-friendly session on AlphaFold and protein folding. The talk introduced the fundamentals of proteins and the long-standing complexity of the folding problem, traced historical approaches to structure prediction, and dived into AlphaFold's revolutionary deep learning architecture. Students gained insight into how open research and open tools have accelerated breakthroughs in biology, with real-world impact on drug discovery and scientific research. The session demonstrated how open-source principles enable cross-disciplinary innovation and global scientific progress.
AlphaFold by DeepMind OpenFold — open source reimplementation Originally posted on the FOSS United Forum.

documents.s: Antitrust Implications of FOSS: A Review

documents.t: The session on Antitrust and Open Source brought together students interested in understanding how competition law interacts with FOSS ecosystems in India. The discussion covered the fundamentals of the Competition Act, insights from the Google Android antitrust case, and emerging questions around fairness, dominance, and openness. The session also examined how the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) impacts FOSS projects and developer responsibilities. Participants engaged deeply with questions about how law influences innovation, collaboration, and corporate involvement in open source — highlighting the growing importance of policy literacy for developers and technologists.
Competition Commission of India Internet Freedom Foundation — DPDP SFLC India Originally posted on the FOSS United Forum.

documents.s: Beyond the Syllabus: Open Source in the Real World

documents.t: We hosted a session on "Open Source and Learning Beyond the Syllabus" conducted by Hari Prasanth S. The session was highly practical and focused on how open source actually works in the real world. Topics covered: Git & GitHub fundamentals How pull requests and contributions work Using MkDocs for documentation How these tools are used in real-world open-source projects The session was open to students from all departments, and it was great to see students asking questions and understanding how open source fits beyond classroom learning. The talk was inspired by the WikiSyllabus initiative — an open-source Wikipedia of university syllabi — which led to great conversations about making education more open. Overall, it was an insightful session and a strong step towards building an open-source culture at Sai University.
WikiSyllabus on GitHub MkDocs FOSS United Forum thread Originally posted on the FOSS United Forum.
Date: September 10, 2025 Format: In-person Venue: SAI University, Chennai

The FOSS Club officially launched on 10th September, with an energetic turnout of students curious about open-source technology and community-driven development. The workshop introduced the core idea of Free and Open-Source Software (FOSS) and explained how global communities collaborate to build impactful software. Participants were introduced to interesting open-source projects and gained an overview of the club's vision and planned activities, including workshops and hands-on sessions. The event also encouraged networking and discussion among students from different backgrounds. Overall, the launch set a positive and welcoming tone for the FOSS Club, laying the foundation for a collaborative space focused on learning, sharing, and building together.
Originally posted on the FOSS United Forum.

documents.s: Hands-on Git & GitHub Workshop for Beginners

documents.t: The FOSS Club of Sai University hosted an engaging hands-on workshop on Git and GitHub, bringing together students eager to strengthen their foundations in version control and collaborative development. The session walked participants through core Git concepts, practical workflows, and real-world collaboration using GitHub. From understanding repositories and commits to exploring how teams contribute to shared codebases, the workshop emphasized why version control is indispensable in modern software development. Students actively experimented, asked thoughtful questions, and gained confidence using tools that power both open-source and industry projects — reinforcing the values of collaboration, transparency, and shared ownership central to open source.
Originally posted on the FOSS United Forum.
Date: November 23, 2025 Format: Online Session Venue: SAI University, Chennai
documents.s: Law in FOSS: Who Owns Open Code?

documents.t: The FOSS Club hosted a thought-provoking online session exploring how legal frameworks intersect with collaborative software development. The discussion unpacked key ideas around copyright in software, clarified what "ownership" means in open source projects, and examined why patenting code is often impractical. Real-world cases such as LinkedIn vs HiQ were used to connect global legal debates with the Indian context. Students gained clarity on the legal implications of sharing code on platforms like GitHub, and were encouraged to think critically about how law can both protect and shape open collaboration.
SFLC India Internet Freedom Foundation Choose a License Creative Commons Licenses Originally posted on the FOSS United Forum.
Date: September 24, 2025 Format: In-person Venue: SAI University, Chennai

The Linux Command Line workshop introduced students to the terminal as a powerful and essential tool for every developer. Designed to be beginner-friendly, the session focused on building comfort through hands-on practice. Participants learned fundamental Linux commands, explored directory structures, and understood how the command line enables efficiency, control, and automation. The workshop highlighted how most open-source development and server environments rely heavily on Linux-based systems. The interactive nature of the workshop encouraged curiosity and experimentation, helping students see the command line as an empowering skill that opens doors to deeper system understanding and open-source contribution.

The FOSS Club maintains and contributes to a number of open source projects. Below are some of our key initiatives.

This very site! A community-maintained wiki built with Docusaurus and hosted on GitHub Pages. Contributions welcome — event writeups, blog posts, resource links, and more. Repository: saiufosswiki Stack: Docusaurus v3, TypeScript, GitHub Pages

If you have an idea for an open source project that benefits the club or campus community, here's how to get started: Open a project proposal issue with a brief description Find collaborators at a club meeting or on our community channels Create a repository under the saiufoss GitHub organisation Add a README, LICENSE (preferably MIT or AGPL), and a CONTRIBUTING guide Announce it on the wiki and blog info All club projects should be open source. We recommend permissive licenses like MIT or Apache 2.0 for software, and CC BY-SA 4.0 for content.
